standard_prerequisites.name: The folding map L from the vertices of the polytope P onto the Boolean lattice, and the vector v defined from the sequence a_i
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up immediately before the counted statement, in the paragraph ending at source line 1412
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects L, v and the increasing sequence a_i in terms of which all four clauses are phrased.

standard_prerequisites.name: The adjacencies of the associahedron are generated by rotating pairs of successive left- and right-leaning edges
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 1430 and 1434-1438
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the author compare two neighbouring trees s and t and compute the edge vector between their images.

core_obligations: Monotonicity: show that switching a pair of successive left- and right-leaning edges to right- and left-leaning ones either preserves the orientation of the leaves or changes exactly one left-leaning leaf into a right-leaning one, whence s <= t implies L(s) <= L(t) (proof line 1430).
Positivity: read the inequality <e_i, v> > 0 off the definition of v (proof line 1432).

Edge direction: reduce to a single polytope K_omega, where t is obtained from s by switching the (i+1)-st leaf from left-leaning to right-leaning, and compute the edge vector explicitly as omega_i omega_{i+2} e_i (proof lines 1434-1438).

Facet containment: in the sequence (1, b_1, ..., b_{n_1-2}, 0) there is an occurrence of (1,0) at some places i, i+1, and every face with L(t) = b lies in the facet labelled by the forest obtained by cutting there (proof line 1439).
proof_roadmap: Argue clause by clause in the order of the statement: the monotonicity from the effect of an edge switch on leaf orientations, positivity from the definition of the vector (proof lines 1430-1432).
Compute the edge vector on one polytope to get the direction, and locate a (1,0) in the folding word to exhibit the facet that contains the fibre (proof lines 1434-1439).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four properties of the folding map L that sends the vertices of the polytope P to the Boolean lattice: monotonicity along the lattice order, positivity of the scalar products with the coordinate vectors, the direction of the edges joining L-fibres, and the containment of every fibre in a facet (statement lines 1414-1425). The proof treats the four clauses separately, and the two that carry content are the third, where the edge vector between two neighbouring trees is computed explicitly as omega_i omega_{i+2} e_i on a single polytope K_omega, and the fourth, where an occurrence of the pattern (1,0) in the folding sequence produces the facet containing the fibre (proof lines 1434-1439). The second clause is dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition of the vector; the first and fourth are argued in one sentence each but with the decisive observation stated. The proof is complete in the sense that every clause is addressed inside the span, so H2.
